blocks.text: Ezekiel 38 presents a prophecy against Gog of the land of Magog, who musters a large military coalition and advances against restored Israel dwelling securely in the land. The Lord declares opposition to Gog and describes divine intervention that will defeat this invasion. The chapter emphasizes divine sovereignty throughout, depicting the Lord taking control of Gog and bringing him forth with his assembled forces to an outcome determined by divine action rather than human calculation.

The textual transmission of this prophecy shows notable variation across ancient manuscript witnesses. Papyrus 967 arranges the material conventionally numbered as Ezekiel 38-39 before chapter 37, diverging from the Masoretic sequence familiar to most readers. The Masoretic text, Old Greek translation, Qumran fragments, and Masada scroll all preserve different wordings and structural arrangements of this material, requiring careful textual analysis at the passage level to understand how this prophecy was transmitted and understood in antiquity.
